claim: The aggregation of the protein α-synuclein is closely associated with several neurodegenerative disorders.
source: The aggregation of the protein α-synuclein is closely associated with several neurodegenerative disorders and as such the structures of the amyloid fibril aggregates have high scientific and medical significance.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about α-synuclein's role in disease.

claim: There are dozens of unique atomic-resolution structures of α-synuclein amyloid fibril aggregates.
source: However, there are dozens of unique atomic-resolution structures of these aggregates, and such a highly polymorphic nature of the α-synuclein fibrils hampers efforts in disease-relevant in vitro studies on α-synuclein amyloid aggregation.
evidence: This is supported by the extensive literature review and citations throughout the manuscript.

claim: In the physiological range of pH 5.8–7.4, a pH-dependent selection between Type 1, 2, and 3 polymorphs occurs.
source: We find that in the physiological range of pH 5.8–7.4, a pH-dependent selection between Type 1, 2, and 3 polymorphs occurs.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by the cryo-EM structural data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Even in the presence of seeds, the polymorph selection during aggregation is highly dependent on the buffer conditions.
source: Our results indicate that even in the presence of seeds, the polymorph selection during aggregation is highly dependent on the buffer conditions, attributed to the non-polymorph-specific nature of secondary nucleation.
evidence: This is supported by the seeding experiments and cryo-EM analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: A monofilament Type 1 fibril that highly resembles the structure of the juvenile-onset synucleinopathy polymorph was found at pH 7.0 in phosphate-buffered saline.
source: The first is a monofilament Type 1 fibril that highly resembles the structure of the juvenile-onset synucleinopathy polymorph found in patient-derived material.
evidence: This is a structural finding supported by cryo-EM data and comparison with published structures.

claim: A new Type 5 polymorph was discovered at pH 7.0 in phosphate-buffered saline.
source: The second is a new Type 5 polymorph that resembles a polymorph that has been recently reported in a study that used diseased tissues to seed aggregation.
evidence: This is a novel structural finding supported by cryo-EM data.

claim: pH plays a major role in polymorph selection and in many cases appears to be the determining factor in seeded aggregation.
source: Taken together, our results highlight the shallow amyloid energy hypersurface that can be altered by subtle changes in the environment, including the pH which is shown to play a major role in polymorph selection and in many cases appears to be the determining factor in seeded aggregation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: All amyloids contain a common structural scaffold known as the cross β-sheet motif.
source: It has long been established that all amyloids contain a common structural scaffold known as the cross β-sheet motif, yet only more recently, with the advent of solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy (NMR) (Meier et al., 2017) and cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) helical reconstruction (He and Scheres, 2017), has it become clear that this shared repetitive motif can generate a wide range of structural folds (Iadanza et al., 2018; Sawaya et al., 2021).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations to the literature.

claim: Amyloid structures derived from a single peptide sequence are often polymorphic.
source: Yet unlike globular proteins, whose amino acid sequence typically guides the protein folding process into a unique 3D structure, the amyloid structures derived from a single peptide sequence are often polymorphic: they can exist in various stable 3D architectures.
evidence: This is established knowledge about amyloid properties.

claim: Amyloid formation is a nucleated growth process analogous to the growth of a 1D crystal.
source: Amyloid formation is a nucleated growth process analogous to the growth of a 1D crystal (Riek and Eisenberg, 2016) and can therefore be kinetically enhanced through templating on preformed fibrillar structures, termed seeds.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Secondary nucleation processes include de novo nuclei formation on the lateral surface of the amyloid fibrils.
source: Additionally, as revealed by kinetic experiments, there are secondary nucleation processes, which include de novo nuclei formation on the lateral surface of the amyloid fibrils (Törnquist et al., 2018).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Amyloid polymorphs with differences in tertiary and quaternary structure display distinct biological activities.
source: Amyloid polymorphs whose differences lie in both their tertiary structure (the arrangement of the β-strands) and the quaternary structure (protofilament-protofilament assembly) have been found to display distinct biological activities (Uemura et al., 2023; Peelaerts et al., 2015; Guo et al., 2013; Van der Perren et al., 2020; Bousset et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to the literature.

claim: Cryo-EM has been used to correlate 14 different tauopathies with distinct combinations of 8 different amyloid polymorphs.
source: In the case of the protein tau, cryo-EM has been used to correlate 14 different tauopathies with distinct combinations of 8 different amyloid polymorphs (Shi et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a specific finding from the literature supported by a citation.

claim: All known in vitro α-synuclein polymorphs are distinct from the polymorphs that have been sarkosyl-extracted from the brains of patients of both multiple systems atrophy (MSA) and Parkinson's disease (PD).
source: In the case of α-synuclein (α-Syn), the structures of many in vitro polymorphs have been determined (Li et al., 2018; Li, 2018; Guerrero-Ferreira et al., 2018; Zhao et al., 2020b; Zhao et al., 2020a; Sun et al., 2020; Ni et al., 2019; Boyer et al., 2019; Guerrero-Ferreira et al., 2019; Boyer et al., 2020; Schweighauser et al., 2020; Long et al., 2021; Sun et al., 2021; Hojjatian et al., 2021; McGlinchey et al., 2021; Lövestam et al., 2021; Frieg et al., 2021; Sun et al., 2023; Zhao et al., 2023; Zhang et al., 2023; Yang et al., 2022; Frieg et al., 2022; Yang et al., 2023; Fan et al., 2023) and yet, they are all distinct from the polymorphs that have been sarkosyl-extracted from the brains of patients of both multiple systems atrophy (MSA) (Schweighauser et al., 2020) and Parkinson's disease (PD) (Yang et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by extensive citations to the literature.

claim: Two MSA polymorphs contain an unidentified molecule at the interface of the protofilaments.
source: Some clues are present in the sarkosyl-insoluble brain-derived structures: two MSA polymorphs contain an unidentified molecule at the interface of the protofilaments and in the PD polymorph an unidentified molecule appears to be stabilizing the structure of the monofilament fibril.
evidence: This is an observation from structural studies of patient-derived material.

claim: In the PD polymorph an unidentified molecule appears to be stabilizing the structure of the monofilament fibril.
source: Some clues are present in the sarkosyl-insoluble brain-derived structures: two MSA polymorphs contain an unidentified molecule at the interface of the protofilaments and in the PD polymorph an unidentified molecule appears to be stabilizing the structure of the monofilament fibril.
evidence: This is an observation from structural studies of patient-derived material.

claim: Prion strains with their specific pathologies can be serially transmitted from animal to animal.
source: Concerning the seeding of polymorphs, it was demonstrated that prion strains with their specific pathologies can be serially transmitted from animal to animal (Prusiner, 1998; Aguzzi and Rajendran, 2009) and that strains can be amplified in vitro by protein misfolding cyclic amplification (PMCA) (Saborio et al., 2001; Soto et al., 2002) or similar approaches (Srivastava et al., 2022).
evidence: This is established knowledge about prions supported by citations.

claim: Prion strains can be amplified in vitro by protein misfolding cyclic amplification (PMCA).
source: Concerning the seeding of polymorphs, it was demonstrated that prion strains with their specific pathologies can be serially transmitted from animal to animal (Prusiner, 1998; Aguzzi and Rajendran, 2009) and that strains can be amplified in vitro by protein misfolding cyclic amplification (PMCA) (Saborio et al., 2001; Soto et al., 2002) or similar approaches (Srivastava et al., 2022).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: In vitro amyloid seeding is not always faithful in reproducing the seed polymorph.
source: However, in vitro, amyloid seeding is not always faithful in reproducing the seed polymorph.
evidence: This is a general observation supported by the examples that follow in the text.

claim: Attempts to amplify the MSA and the PD patient-derived polymorphs in vitro with recombinant α-Syn have resulted in structures distinct from those that were extracted with sarkosyl from patient brains.
source: However, attempts to amplify the MSA and the PD patient-derived polymorphs in vitro with recombinant α-Syn have so far resulted in structures distinct from those that were extracted with sarkosyl from patient brains (Lövestam et al., 2021; Strohäker et al., 2019; Burger et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to the literature.

claim: Secondary nucleation in α-Syn has been shown to involve flexible interactions that might not be able to transmit polymorph-specific structural information.
source: These results could be due to the strong role of secondary nucleation in the in vitro seeding processes, which in the case of α-Syn have been shown to involve flexible interactions that might not be able to transmit polymorph-specific structural information (Gerez and Riek, 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation and represents an interpretation of the literature.

claim: Under conditions of low α-Syn monomer, patient-derived CSF can seed several polymorphs while healthy CSF does not seed amyloid formation at all.
source: Nonetheless, seeding with α-Syn disease-derived amyloids has, at least for cerebrospinal fluid (CSF)-derived seeds, some diagnostic utility as it been shown that under conditions of low α-Syn monomer, patient-derived CSF can seed several polymorphs while healthy CSF does not seed amyloid formation at all (Fan et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to the literature.

claim: The Type 4 polymorph from E46K or G51D mutants can be transmitted to wild-type α-Syn.
source: For example, the Type 4 polymorph from E46K (Long et al., 2021) or G51D (Sun et al., 2021) mutants can be transmitted to wild-type α-Syn, and a polymorph that forms normally only at low salt can be produced at high salt and vice versa by using very high seed concentrations (10%) and by limiting primary and secondary nucleation processes (Bousset et al., 2013; Peduzzo et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to the literature.

claim: At pH 5.8, exclusively the Type 3 structures 3B and 3C were observed.
source: At pH 5.8 we observed exclusively the Type 3 structures 3B and 3C (Figures 3 and 4).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by cryo-EM data shown in Figures 3 and 4.

claim: In the 3C polymorph, the interface contacts are shifted by one residue with respect to 2A and are defined by a salt bridge between E46 and K58 instead of K45 and E57.
source: In its place, we find the 3C polymorph for which the interface contacts are shifted by one residue with respect to 2A and are now defined by a salt bridge between E46 and K58 instead of K45 and E57 (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is a structural observation supported by cryo-EM data and shown in Figure 5B.

claim: In the sample prepared at pH 6.5, a mixture of Types 2 and 3 (2A:2B:3B:3C at 25%:18%:31%:26%) was observed.
source: However, in the sample prepared at pH 6.5, we did indeed see a mixture of Types 2 and 3 (2A:2B:3B:3C at 25%:18%:31%:26%), suggesting that Type 2 is not accessible below pH 6 (Figure 3).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by cryo-EM data shown in Figure 3.

claim: Type 2 is not accessible below pH 6.
source: However, in the sample prepared at pH 6.5, we did indeed see a mixture of Types 2 and 3 (2A:2B:3B:3C at 25%:18%:31%:26%), suggesting that Type 2 is not accessible below pH 6 (Figure 3).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that Type 2 was not found at pH 5.8 but was found at pH 6.5.

claim: The structural basis for the Type 3 preference at lower pH may lie in the protonation state of glutamic acid residues in the vicinity of the C-terminal β-strand (i.e. E83) or of H50.
source: The structural basis for the Type 3 preference at lower pH may lie in the protonation state of glutamic acid residues in the vicinity of the C-terminal β-strand (i.e. E83) or of H50, two regions where polymorphs 2 and 3 are most distinct from each other (discussed below).
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the observed pH-dependence.

claim: In several pH 7.0 aggregation samples, a Type 1 monofilament fibril polymorph (termed 1M) was observed, similar to those from the MSA and Parkinson's-CSF seeding experiments and very similar to the Juvenile-onset synucleinopathy (JOS) polymorph.
source: Therefore, we were surprised to find that in several pH 7.0 aggregation samples (Table 1, Figure 4), we also observed a Type 1 monofilament fibril polymorph (termed 1M), similar to those from the MSA and Parkinson's-CSF seeding experiments and very similar to the Juvenile-onset synucleinopathy (JOS) polymorph (Lövestam et al., 2021; Strohäker et al., 2019; Burger et al., 2021; Figure 6, discussed below).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by cryo-EM data shown in Table 1 and Figures 4 and 6.

claim: A completely new polymorph termed Type 5 was found in one of the pH 7.0 aggregation samples.
source: In yet another of the pH 7.0 aggregation samples we found a completely new polymorph which we have termed Type 5 (Figure 7).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by cryo-EM data shown in Figure 7.

claim: The Type 5 polymorph is unusual in the number of residues that are visible/ordered in the structure, starting from the acetylated N-terminal methionine up until residue 96.
source: Apart from its novel fold, it is unusual in the number of residues that are visible/ordered in the structure, starting from the acetylated N-terminal methionine (buried at the dimer interface) up until residue 96.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryo-EM data.

claim: Type 1 structures were observed almost exclusively above pH 7.0, while Type 2 and 3 structures were observed below pH 7.4 and down to pH 6.5.
source: In particular, we noted that Type 1 structures were observed almost exclusively above pH 7.0, while Type 2 and 3 structures were observed below pH 7.4 and down to pH 6.5.
evidence: This is an observation from the literature review of published structures.

claim: At pH 7.0 in PBS, the samples exhibited a multitude of polymorphs including one having mostly flat (not twisted) fibrils of variable width.
source: Instead, we found that at pH 7.0 in PBS, the samples exhibited a multitude of polymorphs including one having mostly flat (not twisted) fibrils of variable width and the other two each yielding a new polymorph (5A and 1M).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the cryo-EM analysis.

claim: In Tris buffer at pH 7.0, polymorph 1A was produced as the major species.
source: However, in Tris buffer at pH 7.0 we did produce polymorph 1A as the major species.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the cryo-EM analysis.

claim: At pH 7.4 in PBS, polymorph 1A was the dominant species in both samples prepared, even though one was seeded by 5% Type 3 fibrils that had grown at pH 5.8.
source: Returning to PBS but at pH 7.4, polymorph 1A was the dominant species in both samples that we prepared, even though one was seeded by 5% Type 3 fibrils that had grown at pH 5.8 (the latter discussed in more detail below).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the cryo-EM analysis and seeding experiments.

claim: In three pH 7.0 samples, type 2A/B polymorphs were reproduced, two of which also had a significant amount of Type 1M fibrils.
source: In three of these pH 7.0 samples we did finally reproduce the type 2A/B polymorphs (datasets 11–13), two of which also had a significant amount of Type 1M fibrils.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the cryo-EM analysis.

claim: 27 structures of Type 1 polymorphs have been reported, mostly in the pH range of 7.0–7.4 in distinct buffers.
source: 27 structures of Type 1 polymorphs have been reported, mostly in the pH range of 7.0–7.4 in distinct buffers including Tris or phosphate and comprised of full-length α-Syn, N-acetylated α-Syn, shorter constructs (i.e. 1–103, 1–122), familial mutants (i.e. A53T, A53E, H50Q, and a seven residue insertion associated with JOS), patient-derived material (i.e. MSA and JOS), and fibrils that were seeded by MSA, PD, and dementia with Lewy bodies material (including brain or CSF).
evidence: This is a summary of the literature on Type 1 polymorphs.

claim: In the presence of phosphate, the K58 side chain is often facing out toward the 1A protofilament interface, thereby forming a triad with K43 and K45 of the other protofilament to surround some extra density that is interpreted to be phosphate.
source: In the context of how buffer conditions influence the polymorph structure, it is interesting to mention that in the presence of phosphate, the K58 side chain is often facing out toward the 1A protofilament interface, thereby forming a triad with K43 and K45 of the other protofilament to surround some extra density that is interpreted to be phosphate (Figure 8).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the analysis of multiple structures shown in Figure 8.

claim: In phosphate-free conditions (such as Tris, PIPES, or unbuffered) K58 is facing into the core in about two-thirds of a dozen structures, forming a salt bridge/hydrogen bond with E61.
source: In contrast, in phosphate-free conditions (such as Tris, PIPES, or unbuffered) K58 is facing into the core in about two-thirds of a dozen structures, forming a salt bridge/hydrogen bond with E61.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the analysis of multiple structures.

claim: The structures of Type 2 and 3 polymorphs share some similarities, however, there are significant differences that justify their assignment to unique polymorph classes.
source: The structures of Type 2 and 3 polymorphs share some similarities, however, there are significant differences that justify their assignment to unique polymorph classes (Figure 5AB).
evidence: This is a structural analysis supported by the data shown in Figure 5.

claim: There is a displacement of the structural fragment comprising residues V52-T72 which appears to move on the G51 and G73 hinges between Type 2 and Type 3 polymorphs.
source: First, there is a displacement of the structural fragment comprising residues V52-T72 which appears to move on the G51 and G73 hinges.
evidence: This is a structural observation from comparing Type 2 and Type 3 structures.

claim: Only in the Type 2 polymorph can the N-terminal fragment (V15-K21) form an additional β-strand packed against the β-strand A85-A91.
source: The turn with residues G73-A78 is again similar between the two structures but beyond this, there is an 'inside-out' rearrangement of the C-terminal β-strand (A85-G86-S87-I88-A89-A90-A91-T92) such that only in the Type 2 polymorph can the N-terminal fragment (V15-K21) form an additional β-strand packed against the β-strand A85-A91 (Guerrero-Ferreira et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a structural observation supported by a citation.

claim: The Type 3B structure has characteristics of a pseudo-21 helical symmetry (ca. 179.5° twist and 2.35 Å rise) when refined under C1 symmetry with a ca. –1° twist and 4.7 Å rise.
source: Our data shows the characteristics of a pseudo-21 helical symmetry (ca. 179.5° twist and 2.35 Å rise) when refined under C1 symmetry with a ca. –1° twist and 4.7 Å rise (Figure 9) while the MSA-seeded Type 3B structure (PDB entry 7NCG) has a C2 symmetry (–0.95° twist 4.75 Å rise).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryo-EM data shown in Figure 9.

claim: The MSA-seeded Type 3B structure (PDB entry 7NCG) has a C2 symmetry (–0.95° twist 4.75 Å rise).
source: Our data shows the characteristics of a pseudo-21 helical symmetry (ca. 179.5° twist and 2.35 Å rise) when refined under C1 symmetry with a ca. –1° twist and 4.7 Å rise (Figure 9) while the MSA-seeded Type 3B structure (PDB entry 7NCG) has a C2 symmetry (–0.95° twist 4.75 Å rise).
evidence: This is a structural observation from a published structure.

claim: The interfaces present in the 2A and 3C polymorphs consist of a pair of symmetric salt bridges arranged to create a large solvent-filled cavity at the interface.
source: The interfaces present in the 2A and 3C polymorphs also appear to be similar at first glance, consisting of a pair of symmetric salt bridges arranged to create a large solvent-filled cavity at the interface.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryo-EM data.

claim: The 2A and 3C interfaces comprise neighboring sets of E/K residues: K45/E57 in 2A and E46/K58 in 3C.
source: However, a close inspection reveals that they are different, comprising neighboring sets of E/K residues: K45/E57 in 2A and E46/K58 in 3C.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryo-EM data.

claim: E46K fibrils produced at pH 5.8 yielded a Type 3 polymorph with a new interface termed 3D formed by an E57/K58 salt bridge.
source: To test this further, we produced E46K fibrils at pH 5.8, the condition where until now only Type 3 has been observed and uncovered yet another Type 3 polymorph with a new interface termed 3D formed by an E57/K58 salt bridge (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by cryo-EM data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The coexistence of polymorphs 2A/2B and 3B/3C at pH 6.5 indicates either that they all have a similar thermodynamic stability or that some of them are kinetically trapped.
source: Finally, the coexistence of polymorphs 2A/2B and 3B/3C at pH 6.5 indicates either that they all have a similar thermodynamic stability or that some of them are kinetically trapped, the latter possibility having been observed in one case of two distinct α-Syn polymorphs grown in a single condition (10 mM Tris, 0.02% NaN3, pH 7.0 at 37°C) (Pálmadóttir et al., 2023).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation of multiple polymorphs coexisting, supported by a citation.

claim: Polymorph 5A is unusual in the number of residues that are visible/ordered in the structure, starting from the acetylated N-terminal methionine (buried at the dimer interface) up until residue E96.
source: Apart from its novel fold, polymorph 5A is unusual in the number of residues that are visible/ordered in the structure, starting from the acetylated N-terminal methionine (buried at the dimer interface) up until residue E96.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryo-EM data.

claim: In the Type 5 structure, residues 47–72, comprising a two β-strand motif with a turn in between, overlay very well with the polymorph formed by a Y39 phosphorylated α-Syn.
source: In particular, residues 47–72, comprising a two β-strand motif with a turn in between, overlay very well with the polymorph formed by a Y39 phosphorylated α-Syn (Zhao et al., 2020b) and to a lesser extent in Types 2, 3, and 4 as well.
evidence: This is a structural comparison supported by a citation.

claim: Within the first 35 residues of Type 5, there are seven lysine and five glutamic/aspartic acid residues and five of the lysine residues are buried inside the structure and form salt bridges with buried glutamic/aspartic acid residues.
source: Within this segment, there are seven lysine and five glutamic/aspartic acid residues and five of the lysine residues are buried inside the structure and form salt bridges with buried glutamic/aspartic acid residues.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryo-EM data.

claim: The Type 5 structure has two large cavities separated only by the very polar segment G31-K32-T33-K34-E35-G36, and it is likely that these two cavities are filled with water.
source: This yields two large cavities separated only by the very polar segment G31-K32-T33-K34-E35-G36, and it is likely that these two cavities are filled with water.
evidence: This is a structural observation and inference from the cryo-EM data.

claim: The Type 5 structure was found in only one sample at pH 7.0, and then, in only 10–20% of the observed fibrils in the sample.
source: It is also worth mentioning that in the 10 independent aggregations that we analyzed at pH 7.0, the Type 5 structure was found in only one sample, and then, in only 10–20% of the observed fibrils in the sample.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the cryo-EM analysis.

claim: The presence of seed fibrils consistently accelerated the aggregation of α-Syn.
source: In terms of kinetics, the presence of seed fibrils consistently accelerated the aggregation of α-Syn (Figure 10A).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the ThT fluorescence kinetics experiments shown in Figure 10A.

claim: In the cryo-EM analyses of the fibrils produced at pH 5.8 with pH 7.4 seeds, only the polymorphs 3B and 3C are detected.
source: However, in the cryo-EM analyses of the fibrils produced at pH 5.8 with pH 7.4 seeds, only the polymorphs 3B and 3C are detected (Figure 10B) and in the inverse case, with fibrils produced at pH 7.4 with pH 5.8 seeds only polymorph 1A is detected (Figure 10B).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the cryo-EM analysis shown in Figure 10B.

claim: In fibrils produced at pH 7.4 with pH 5.8 seeds, only polymorph 1A is detected.
source: However, in the cryo-EM analyses of the fibrils produced at pH 5.8 with pH 7.4 seeds, only the polymorphs 3B and 3C are detected (Figure 10B) and in the inverse case, with fibrils produced at pH 7.4 with pH 5.8 seeds only polymorph 1A is detected (Figure 10B).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the cryo-EM analysis shown in Figure 10B.

claim: No traces of the seed polymorphs were detected in either of the cross-seeded aggregations despite the fact that 5% seeds were used.
source: We were unable to detect any traces of the seed polymorphs in either of the cross-seeded aggregations despite the fact that 5% seeds were used.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the cryo-EM analysis.

claim: LiP-MS analysis revealed that fibrils generated at pH 7.4 (F3) and pH 5.8 (F4), in the presence of unfragmented fibrillar seeds generated at pH 5.8 and pH 7.4 respectively, are on average more similar in their structure to the fibrils generated without seeds at pH 7.4 (F1) and pH 5.8 (F2), respectively.
source: LiP-MS analysis revealed that fibrils generated at pH 7.4 (F3) and pH 5.8 (F4), in the presence of unfragmented fibrillar seeds generated at pH 5.8 and pH 7.4 respectively, are on average more similar in their structure to the fibrils generated without seeds at pH 7.4 (F1) and pH 5.8 (F2), respectively (Figure 10C).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the LiP-MS analysis shown in Figure 10C.

claim: Fibrillar conformations resulting from seeding monomeric α-Syn with unfragmented fibrillar seeds are driven by pH and not by the structure of the seed.
source: These data suggest that fibrillar conformations resulting from seeding monomeric α-Syn with unfragmented fibrillar seeds are driven by pH and not by the structure of the seed.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the LiP-MS and cryo-EM data.

claim: In fibril elongation, the incoming protein adopts the conformation of the seed by attaching itself to the end of the fibril.
source: In fibril elongation, the incoming protein adopts the conformation of the seed by attaching itself to the end of the fibril.
evidence: This is established knowledge about amyloid fibril growth mechanisms.

claim: In the process of fibril elongation, which is proportional to the number of fibril ends, the polymorph structure is expected to be preserved.
source: In this process of growth acceleration, which is proportional to the number of fibril ends, the polymorph structure is expected to be preserved (Jarrett and Lansbury, 1993; Jarrett and Lansbury, 1992).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: In the secondary nucleation process, de novo aggregation occurs on the sides of the fibril and therefore the kinetics of secondary nucleation is proportional to the mass of the fibril.
source: In the secondary nucleation process, de novo aggregation occurs on the sides of the fibril and therefore the kinetics of secondary nucleation is proportional to the mass of the fibril (Knowles et al., 2007).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: The secondary nucleation mechanism in α-Syn has been proposed to be based on the interaction of the positively charged N-terminal region of monomeric α-Syn and the disordered, negatively charged C-terminal region of the α-Syn amyloid fibrils.
source: In the case of α-Syn, the secondary nucleation mechanism has been proposed to be based on the interaction of the positively charged N-terminal region of monomeric α-Syn and the disordered, negatively charged C-terminal region of the α-Syn amyloid fibrils (Kumari et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism supported by a citation.

claim: Since all known amyloid polymorphs of α-Syn are disordered in their C-terminal regions, secondary nucleation in α-Syn aggregation is generally polymorph unspecific.
source: Since all known amyloid polymorphs of α-Syn are disordered in their C-terminal regions, we propose that secondary nucleation in α-Syn aggregation is generally polymorph unspecific.
evidence: This is a proposal/inference based on structural knowledge and the mechanism of secondary nucleation.

claim: At lower seed concentrations under which secondary nucleation dominates over fibril elongation, the environment dictates the resulting polymorph.
source: This conclusion is consistent with those of Peduzzo et al., 2020, who showed that at lower seed concentrations under which secondary nucleation dominates over fibril elongation, the environment dictates the resulting polymorph.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to the literature.

claim: Unfragmented fibrils will likely favor secondary nucleation, while with shorter fibrils and more available ends per unit mass, elongation could dominate.
source: It is worth noting that unfragmented fibrils will likely favor secondary nucleation, while with shorter fibrils and more available ends per unit mass, elongation could dominate.
evidence: This is an inference based on the mechanisms of fibril growth.

claim: Strohäker et al., 2019, used NMR to analyze the results of PMCA using both PD and MSA seed material in PBS buffer at pH 7.4 in the presence of 1% Triton X-100, and both samples yielded indistinguishable polymorphs.
source: In addition to the α-Syn seeding experiments discussed until now, Strohäker et al., 2019, used NMR to analyze the results of PMCA using both PD and MSA seed material in PBS buffer at pH 7.4 in the presence of 1% Triton X-100. Both samples yielded indistinguishable polymorphs.
evidence: This is a finding from the literature supported by a citation.

claim: Burger et al., 2021, use both MSA and PD patient-derived material to produce a new polymorph which they name Type 6, and a similar Type 6 fold was obtained irrespective of whether the starting material was from an MSA or PD patient brain.
source: In another PMCA study that is published currently only on the BioRxiv server, Burger et al., 2021, use both MSA and PD patient-derived material to produce a new polymorph which they name Type 6. A similar Type 6 fold was obtained irrespective of whether the starting material was from an MSA or PD patient brain, however protofilaments were arranged in a disease-specific manner.
evidence: This is a finding from the literature supported by a citation.

claim: The Type 6 fold resembles the Type 5 that was found at pH 7.0.
source: Interestingly, the Type 6 fold resembles the Type 5 that we found at pH 7.0, deviating however in its three different protofilament interfaces yielding polymorphs 6A, 6B, and 6C as well as extra density that the authors have assigned to the C-terminal residues.
evidence: This is a comparison between the authors' findings and those from the literature.

claim: Seeding experiments with α-Syn can be very sensitive to the environment and it is a multifactorial problem where there is not a single optimal pH or optimal salt condition.
source: The results indicate that seeding experiments with α-Syn can be very sensitive to the environment and that it is a multifactorial problem where there is not a single optimal pH or optimal salt condition.
evidence: This is a conclusion from a study cited in the manuscript.
